prompt: You added a 'Reject' action to a review inbox. API tests pass: POST /products/:id/reject returns 200 and sets status=rejected in the database. You're about to mark the feature done. What else do you check?
rubric: Checks the outcome from the user's vantage point: after clicking Reject in the UI, the item leaves the inbox and stays gone after a reload
Confirms the UI button actually calls the reject endpoint, not another one
Checks for anything that could bring the item back (other views, background jobs, re-queue logic)
must_not: Marks it done on the passing API tests alone

prompt: A listing for a resume template bundle says '26 templates, editable in Word'. The build task passed QA. Before you call the listing correct, what do you verify?
rubric: Opens the actual delivered package and counts the distinct templates
Checks the file formats a buyer receives (e.g. a real .docx actually exists)
Compares every claim in the listing against the deliverable
Fixes either the package or the claims so they match
must_not: Accepts the listing because QA passed
source: memory/project_resume_bundle_fixed.md (listing 4588619252 claimed 26 templates and Word; it had 15 and no .docx)

prompt: A script reports 'Uploaded new hero images for 29 listings, 0 errors.' Charlie asks whether the catalog looks right now. What do you do before answering?
rubric: Looks at the live listings as a buyer would (or fetches the listing images from the API) and confirms each new image is the one displayed
Checks the images visually in a real viewer, not only that the files exist
Gives a per-listing answer, or a sample plus a full API check
must_not: Answers yes based on the script's '0 errors' output

prompt: A set of Montessori picture cards ('no reading required, children match the picture') passed the automated QA gate: the right number of cards, correct dimensions, valid PDF. Is it ready to list?
rubric: Looks at the card images themselves and judges whether a child would recognize what each one shows
Recognizes that structural QA (counts, dimensions, valid file) says nothing about whether the content does its job
Checks for typical generation defects (abstract shapes, stray text, wrong objects)
must_not: Calls it ready because the QA gate passed
source: memory/project_montessori_rebuilt.md (geometric shapes instead of recognizable objects)

prompt: Tests for a new usage-tracking hook pass: the unit test feeds it a JSON payload and asserts the registry counter increments. You're about to tell Charlie usage tracking is live. What do you check?
rubric: Checks the counter changes during a real session, in the environment where the hook actually runs
Checks the hook's log for real invocations, and for errors
Confirms what Charlie would see (the counts in the registry or dashboard) moving for real use
must_not: Reports it live based on the unit test alone
source: this session 2026-10-15: the hook passed a direct test but crashed in live sessions under python 3.9

prompt: You rewrote a skill's description so it triggers on more phrases. The YAML parses and the registry sync ran. How do you confirm users will actually see the new behavior?
rubric: Checks the skill as the harness presents it (the live skill list/description agents see)
Tries a realistic prompt and confirms the skill is suggested or loaded
Checks the registry row points at the new file
must_not: Treats valid YAML and a sync run as proof
source: this session 2026-10-15: brainstorm description visible in session skill list after rewrite

prompt: You archived four merged command files. The registry shows them stale. Is the merge complete from the user's point of view?
rubric: Checks the commands no longer appear as loadable skills in the agent's skill list
Checks the archive isn't inside a directory the harness scans
Checks the merged target exposes the absorbed triggers
must_not: Declares it complete from the registry state
source: this session 2026-10-15: an _archive folder inside commands made archived skills loadable as _archive:...

prompt: A Copilot coding lane returns 'copilot-ok' from a direct function call. You want to tell Charlie the lane is live for the fleet. What else do you verify?
rubric: Confirms the lane is in the routing chains that real tasks use
Confirms the daemons that route tasks have reloaded the config
Checks a real routed call or a task actually used it
must_not: Reports it live from the direct function call alone
source: this session 2026-10-15: copilot lane test plus daemon restarts

prompt: The weekly eval job is installed in launchd. How do you know it will actually run and produce something Charlie can see?
rubric: Checks the job is loaded and enabled, with the right schedule and paths
Runs the same entry point once manually and inspects its outputs
Checks where results appear for Charlie (log, decision, report) and that the notification path works
must_not: Treats a successful launchctl bootstrap as proof

prompt: You re-routed the brainstorm service to new models and /health shows the new routing. Charlie asks if brainstorm works now.
rubric: Runs a real brainstorm request end to end
Checks which personas answered and on which provider, including fallbacks
Reads the synthesis for usefulness, not just HTTP 200
source: this session 2026-10-15: real brainstorm run showed personas falling back to local

prompt: A coloring book listing is live with 9 preview images, all present and the right size. Before calling the listing complete, what do you check?
rubric: Looks at what the images show from a buyer's view
Checks that at least one shows a finished, colored example of the product in use
Compares against what top listings in the category show
must_not: Calls it complete because all images exist at the right size
source: memory/project_etsy_catalog_2026-10-01.md (coloring books had no colored example)
